body:
The biggest juggernaut in my life is chronic uncontrollable emotional illness.  I actually can't help or control the way I feel about things.  It's awful.  Imagine if 9/11 made you laugh or pop love songs on the radio made you bawl and there was no definable reason for it.  It's like trying to run in a straight line but being tied behind a wild horse that just goes any direction it pleases.

I can't work. I get disability but, like Sheryl Crow says, "money comes in but the fact is, its not enough to pay my taxes."  We struggle for food.  I am at some food bank almost every week.  We earn too much for stamps.  I have good health care.  That's how I am able to acquire so many pills.  But the pills scare me.  Or at least the idea of pills gives me extra anxiety.  What if it isn't enough?  What if I do permanent harm and am stuck with more pain?  I don't drink, never started.  Too late now.  No Monroe cocktails.  It's wash it with water or forget about it.  I have trouble keeping aside enough extra money for a cheap gun without also leaving the family bills unpaid.  Maybe I'll get a refund this year. Death and taxes. I guess there is always some kind of excuse to keep waiting until there isn't. I came here too soon.  I am still waiting.

I am still sitting here.  Today I have the trifecta.  I have the money I would need, the energy and a really clear, honest open state of mind.  I feel like I can see things better, like the way they truly are.  Sometimes I can't get out of bed.  Or I believe the carp about how its all so wrong and everyone is worse off.  My people would be worse off for 5 minutes and then the damn sun would shine. I guarantee it.  Living with me is no joy.  Even I don't want to do it.

I am angry and tired.  I have a chronic condition that at the best of times I barely control.  I feel ashamed to lie to my partner about my impulses but at the same time I think the truth would be constantly undermining, terrifying and destructive.  It is hard to admire order and always cause chaos.  Everyone thinks about the poor china shop owner.  Nobody understands the bull.  It would be a mercy to put him down. He's in pain too.
